argument.text: Fix tau>0 and real alpha,beta. If either phase is zero the definition of eta gives zero. Otherwise put hcov(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-M_tau(exp(-i*alpha*s)), with s in [0,tau]. Then eta=tau^(-1)integral hcov(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The identity hcov(s)=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau(exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r))dr and the bound |exp(ix)-exp(iy)|<=|x-y| give |hcov(s)|<=tau*|alpha|, and more precisely |hcov(0)|+|hcov(tau)|<=tau*|alpha|. Also integral_0^tau |hcov'(s)|ds=tau*|alpha|. Taking absolute values gives |eta|<=tau|alpha|. Integrating the beta exponential once gives |eta|<=(|hcov(0)|+|hcov(tau)|+integral|hcov'|)/(tau|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta|. Interchanging phases proves both asserted minima. All integrations are of smooth scalar functions on a compact interval.

For nonzero integers a+b+c+d=0 the largest magnitude is at most the sum of the other three, hence N1<=3N2. Put A=|ab|, B=|cd|. If |d| is one of the two largest magnitudes, min(A/B,B/A)<=1 gives the first majorant. Otherwise the two largest are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, use B/A to get (1/|d|)min(A/B,B/A)<=|c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio is between 1/3 and 3, so the expression is <=3 min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3: use its second entry when |b|>=|d| and its first entry otherwise. The pair b,c is identical by interchanging a,b.

produces.statement: For these nonzero zero-sum frequencies, N1<=3N2 and (1/|d|)min(A/B,B/A)<=3/N3.

argument.text: For the second majorant, if the two largest magnitudes are in the same pair of (a,b),(c,d), the other pair has sum magnitude <=2N3. Since a+b=-(c+d), the quotient |a+b|/max(A,B)<=2N3/(N1*N2)<=2/N3. If they lie in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, so max(A,B)>=N2*N3, while |a+b|<=2N1<=6N2. Thus the quotient is <=6/N3. Ties may be ordered arbitrarily and are included in these alternatives. These arguments prove the universal assertions with no remaining assumptions.
